sentences.text: This dinosaur is defined by the tall neural spines running along its back.
Its upper jaw held nineteen curved, serrated teeth on each side.
The biggest known individual measured between 11 and 11.5 meters long and weighed from 4.4 to 8.4 metric tons.
J. Willis Stovall and Wann Langston Jr. created the name Acrocanthosaurus in 1950.
Fossils were originally unearthed within the Antlers Formation of Oklahoma.
Scientists recovered a nearly complete skeleton nicknamed Fran from that same formation.
It likely acted as an apex predator hunting sauropods, ornithopods, and ankylosaurs.
Research estimates its bite force reached 8,266 newtons at the front and 16,894 newtons at the rear of the jaws.
Bone evidence indicates it required at least 12 years to reach full maturity.
Taxonomists place it in the superfamily Allosauroidea and the infraorder Tetanurae.
Most modern studies assign it to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
The animal lived from the Barremian to the Cenomanian stages of the Early and Late Cretaceous.
This corresponds to a time between 125 and 99.6 million years ago.
Experts disagree on whether fossils from the Cloverly Formation belong to this species.
One biomechanical study argues that running at high speeds may have been impossible for it.
Some researchers from the 1980s thought its tall vertebrae linked it to the family Spinosauridae.
In 1988, Gregory S. Paul named a second species, A. altispinax, based on similar tall spined vertebrae found in England.
